correctness.rationale: In an oriented tree, if \(x<y<z\) in reachability order, the directed \(x\)-to-\(y\) and \(y\)-to-\(z\) paths cannot share an edge with opposite traversal and concatenate to the unique underlying \(x\)-to-\(z\) tree path; therefore that path is directed and, because no alternative route exists, geodesic. Conversely any directed geodesic containing three selected vertices orders them into a three-element reachability chain. Hence directed general-position sets are exactly two-families. Greene–Kleitman at \(k=2\) then gives the chain-partition min–max formula. The bundled exhaustive replay through six vertices is a stress test, not the universal proof.

final_claim: For every finite oriented tree, directed general-position sets are exactly the two-families of its reachability poset, so the general-position number equals the Greene–Kleitman minimum over chain partitions of the sum of \(\min\{2,|C|\}\).
limitations: No unchanged extension to general DAGs with directed shortcuts is claimed.
